properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the loop's `next` is a fixed sequence of design-phase debt written in code, and what an operations ranking needs is either not recorded or not read. A Project cannot declare a phase (mode is governance only, flexible or rigid, and "operations" is refused). A finding carries no safety mark. Open defect findings and failing checks are never lines of `next`. So a safety item is not outranked: it is absent
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, 2026-09-28, reflow2 0.73.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. Issue F-33.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "Design-completeness gaps drown the operations signal. loop_status: 43 gaps never put to the user, 16 structural defects, 6 questions asked on 2026-08-26 and never answered. For an operations user, 'which quality attribute is this for' and 'what drawing standard' will never be answered, and every session pays for reading past them. Meanwhile the safety-relevant item of the day (a possible brake gas leak on a detector axis that may be vertical) has no way to outrank them, because it is not in the graph at all (F-30)." EXPECTED: in a project that is operating, the loop's first line is what matters to operations now (an open incident, a failing check, a safety concern), and design-completeness questions do not repeat on every read. NOT AFFECTED: the counts are correct. since_export already narrows to what a session introduced, and a contributor-scoped call narrows to assigned decisions.

② PRECEDENT:
· fact:the-defect-count-is-severity-blind-so-parked-ideas-are-reported-as-outstanding-debt: this hub's F-03 and F-11, 2026-09-10; a distinction computed and then discarded at the reporting boundary.
· This hub's F-14 (2026-09-10): "the same lines on every one of ~15 calls ... while the user was mid-task at a beamline", asking for a session snooze or a since-last-call view.
· req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes (proposed, triple-corroborated; since_export is built), and dec:idea-scoping-exists-and-did-not-narrow-what-a-builder-sees.
· dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing (accepted 2026-08-19): Anthony chose "detecting is not asking" over "a user-set posture, a computed phase, and full lifecycle phases — all of which ask the user to declare something".
· dec:defects-are-temporal-facts: its reader was left owed.

③ CANDIDATES:
(A) ORDER. `next` is built in a fixed order in code, and nothing a project records changes it.
(B) NO PHASE. A project cannot say it is in operations. set_project_mode, the place the reporter names, may carry something else.
(C) THE OPERATIONS SIGNAL IS NOT IN THE LIST. What O-20 wants first (open incidents, failing or stale checks, safety findings) is not a line of `next` at all.
(D) NO SAFETY MARK on a finding.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. A quieting path exists (acknowledge the gaps, withdraw the stale questions) and was not used.
(F) OUTSIDE REFLOW2. The harness or the hub's hooks call loop_status on every orientation and read `next` aloud, so the repetition is theirs.

④ SEPARATING: A predicts `next` is built by unconditional pushes in a fixed sequence. B predicts set_project_mode refuses a phase. C predicts no `next` line for an open defect finding or a failing check. D predicts no safety-valued field on TemporalFact. E predicts a way to say, once, that a class of question does not apply to this project. F cannot be refuted from here, but it does not predict A to D.

⑤ RESULTS (code at v0.74.0, 70e547f, plus a scratch store on the 0.74.0 binary):
· report.rs builds `next` by unconditional pushes in one sequence: waiting questions, answered questions with an open gap, assigned decisions, unsurfaced gaps, structural defects, unproven capabilities, undispositioned drift, unexamined claims, follow-ups, deferrals, then the "no real result" line. No input reorders it. A contributor scope replaces the list; it does not reorder it. A HOLDS.
· set_project_mode with mode "operations" returned: "Validation error on Project.mode: invalid enum value 'operations', expected one of [flexible, rigid]". The schema says mode is governance only, deciding whether apply_heal applies repairs or proposes them: "That one gate is ALL this currently changes". No Project property records a lifecycle phase. B HOLDS.
· An open defect finding on the scratch Project produced no `next` line. Failing checks, and checks with a re-run owed, appear only in the `verifications` digest (`attention`, `rerun_owed`), never as a `next` line. On reflow2's own design, 349 defect findings carry no valid_to and none reaches `next`. C HOLDS.
· `concern` (which has a `safety` value) is declared on Requirement and Constraint, and EnvironmentRule has rule_type `safety`. TemporalFact declares no such field. D HOLDS for findings: today a safety concern can be marked only by writing it as a Requirement or a Constraint.
· Quieting: acknowledge_gaps takes a reason PER ITEM by design ("a batch under one shared reason would be the silent bulk accept this refuses to be"; dec:bulk-keeps-the-judgement-per-item). An acknowledgement expires when its affected nodes change, and nothing lets a project rule a whole KIND of gap out of scope. withdraw_question exists for the six stale questions. E is QUALIFIED: the questions could have been withdrawn in six calls, but the 43 gaps need 43 reasons and would come back as the design moves.
⇒ A, B, C and D hold and are one cause: the loop's priority is fixed in code from the design phase's point of view, and the facts an operations ranking would need are either not recorded (the phase, a safety mark on a finding) or recorded and not read (open defect findings, failing checks). E narrows the cause but does not refute it.

⑥ CLASS: the class of fact:the-defect-count-is-severity-blind-so-parked-ideas-are-reported-as-outstanding-debt, one rung further. The loop's summary is blind to phase and urgency the way that count was blind to severity, and here the distinction is not even recorded. Test: a fix at the class (the loop ranks by something the project declares or records as urgent) would also have answered this hub's F-14 of 2026-09-10 and F-11's "reads as debt". since_export, built for req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes, answered neither, because it narrows by session, not by what matters now.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE: no code changed. A test pinning the class would assert three things. First, a recorded open defect finding and a failing check each appear in the loop's ranked output. Second, something the design records (a declared phase, or an urgency) can change the order of `next`, and the change is visible. Third, a kind of gap the owner has ruled out of scope once is not listed on every call, and the ruling itself is visible.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS. HELD: the counts repeat on every read, and a safety item cannot outrank them. QUALIFIED: "set_project_mode already exists" (O-20); it does, but it is governance, not phase. "Because it is not in the graph at all" was true that day, but even a recorded defect finding would not have outranked the gaps, because the loop reads none. The idea is O-20, recorded separately.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
· the hub's actual gap mix, meaning which of the 43 are design-completeness kinds and which touch operations (its graph was not read);
· whether the harness or the hub's hooks amplify the repetition (candidate F);
· whether an operator would declare a phase and keep it current. dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing chose not to ask users to declare one, for a different complaint.
